Subject: Cost pressure: quick question on per-token parity with cloud endpoints

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profiles and the per-route observability. We're in the middle of an internal procurement review and cost modeling exercise. Two quick asks: 1) do you have a public playbook for matching per-token economics to the major cloud LLM endpoints (OpenAI / Anthropic) for hosted usage? 2) If we commit to a 12-month spend band, what kind of per-token breakpoints and guaranteed SLOs would you offer?

We ran a rough forecast and our projected steady-state traffic is ~1.2B tokens/mo (mix of gen/chat/embeddings), with spiky peaks up to 2.5B. Our procurement team will expect comparable unit costs to the cloud providers and a simple, auditable commit.

I attached our spend runbook for context. Can you send a high-level counter so we can feed it into our procurement model?

— Eva

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>

Cc: Tyler Ng <tyler@bluepeak.com>

Subject: Re: Cost pressure: quick question on per-token parity with cloud endpoints

Hi Eva — great to hear the demo resonated. Appreciate the runbook; useful signal on traffic shape. Below is a concise counterproposal and rationale so you can drop it into procurement.

High-level counter (starter):
- Anchor: list price hosted per-token: $0.00012 / input-token, $0.00024 / output-token (model family X2 equivalent).
- 12-month committed bands (monthly average tokens):
  * 250M+ : 12% discount vs list
  * 750M+ : 18% discount vs list
  * 1.5B+ : 26% discount vs list + committed burst pool (20% of commit)
- Overages: charged at list * (1 - band%) for tokens above committed average; burst pools help cover monthly spikes.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability SLA for dedicated route; 95th pct latency targets provided per model in the proposal.
- Commercials: 30-day billing cadence, quarterly usage true-ups; early-termination: pro-rated usage charge for months used.

Why this structure: we tune effective unit economics by blending a guaranteed commit with a small burst buffer so you don't hit overage cliffs during seasonality. Compared to public cloud endpoints:
- OpenAI/Anthropic list rates are often lower at small volumes but lack predictable committed-burst contracts at enterprise scale; we compete on predictable unit cost at scale, routing controls, and observability that reduce your margin of error.
- With a 1.2B steady-state, the 26% band yields materially lower effective per-token than on-demand cloud for most gen-heavy workloads when you include cacheable prefix reuse and KV cache benefits.

I've attached a working proposal spreadsheet with the band math and a sample invoice cadence. Happy to walk procurement through the model this week.

Next steps: tell me which band you want priced into a formal PO (250M / 750M / 1.5B) and if you need a DocuSign-ready SOW.

— Alex

Subject: Fwd: BluePeak cost pressure: procurement price-match ask (DP-4928) — need approval

Team — forwarding BluePeak procurement's ask. Key points: they want a documented price-match clause (first 6 months) against OpenAI/Anthropic blended on-demand if we can show better effective per-token. Traffic mix: gen/chat/embeds, ~1.2B avg, peaks to 2.5B. They suggest 12-month commit.

My recommended response:
- Offer firm 6-month price parity guard that guarantees effective per-token <= competitor benchmark for the first 6 months but with negotiated guardrails:
  1) Benchmark definition: OpenAI/Anthropic published list rates for comparable model family, plus documented platform fees; use monthly blended on-demand calculation from their bill as the audit source.
  2) Cap on currency: parity applies only to token volumes up to 1.5B/mo equivalent; above that we revert to agreed tiered bands.
  3) Audit process: BluePeak provides redacted invoice excerpt (monthly aggregate tokens and blended rate). We compare using our audited meter; any discrepancy triggers true-up credit to BluePeak at month-end.
  4) Mutual right to request proof for a single month if either party suspects gaming (redacted line-items fine).
- Commercial quid pro quo: in exchange for the parity guard, we ask for a 12-month committed minimum with a 20% non-refundable upfront credit applied to first two invoices (reduces churn risk).

Rationale: preserves our margin if they shift large burst beyond modeled commit, gives procurement the comparative guard they want, and gives us cash/security.

Vivek/Laura — thoughts on legal and margin impact? I flagged DP-4928 as medium strategic (reference: similar displacement opportunity in Q2 last year).

— Alex

Hi Eva / Tyler — thanks for the clear ask and patience while we scoped internally. Below is a formal counter we can put into an SOW and DocuSign packet. We think this balances your procurement requirement for parity with our need to protect committed economics.

Formal counter (DP-4928):
- Term: 12 months, effective on DocuSign signature date.
- Commit: 1.2B tokens/month average (12-mo). Monthly true-ups; overages billed per the band rate.
- Pricing bands (post-discount effective list):
  * Core commit (1.2B): effective blended unit = list * 0.74 (26% discount).
  * Allowed burst pool: 20% of monthly commit for free (consumed before overage).
- Price-match guard (first 6 months only):
  * We will guarantee effective per-token <= publicly published OpenAI/Anthropic on-demand blended rate for a like-for-like model family, up to 1.5B tokens in a month.
  * Verification: BluePeak will provide a redacted monthly invoice summary (aggregate tokens and blended on-demand rate). Redwood will compare against our meter; any shortfall will be credited on the next invoice.
  * Guard caveats: parity applies only to token economics (not to feature parity like fine-tuning or tooling). Parity doesn't apply if BluePeak runs >3x spike relative to their monthly average for >2 consecutive months (we'll re-review).
- Commercial trade: 20% non-refundable upfront credit applied to the first two invoices ($X credit on signature). Standard 30-day invoice terms.
- Termination: pro-rated refund of unused upfront credit if Redwood terminates for cause.

Attachments: final proposal spreadsheet + DocuSign SOW; if acceptable we'll issue the DocuSign link within 24 hours and lock these rates for 48 hours pending signature.

Open items: whether we need legal to add additional audit language or stricter anti-gaming clauses. Laura/Vivek — happy to fold in any edits.

If this looks reasonable, Eva, tell me which billing string you prefer and we'll route the DocuSign packet.

Best,
